create.name: Damien Echols
create.bio:
Damien Echols spent almost eighteen years on Arkansas's death row as one of the West Memphis Three before his release in 2011, and he has said that a daily practice of ceremonial magick is what kept him alive and sane through those years, much of it in solitary confinement. His path draws on the Western Hermetic tradition: the Qabalah, ritual work such as the Lesser Banishing Ritual of the Pentagram, energy work, meditation and inner alchemy. Since leaving prison he has also trained in the Korean martial art Tang Soo Do, which now shapes his teaching on discipline and presence.

He writes and teaches in plain, questioning language, presenting magick as a practice to test for yourself rather than a creed. His books include the memoir Life After Death, High Magick, Angels and Archangels, Ritual (written with his wife, Lorri Davis) and The Alchemy of the Broken Blade, which joins Hermetic alchemy with the step-by-step spirit of kaizen. He posts teaching videos on YouTube and to members on Patreon, and leads retreats in New York's Hudson Valley that combine sitting meditation, talks on the Great Work and a sword form practised as moving meditation.

books.title: High Magick: A Guide to the Spiritual Practices That Saved My Life on Death Row
books.author: Damien Echols
books.description: An introduction to Western ceremonial magick based on the practices Echols kept up in prison: the Qabalah, the Middle Pillar, banishing rituals, energy work and meditation. Eddie Vedder wrote the foreword.

books.title: Angels and Archangels: A Magician's Guide
books.author: Damien Echols
books.description: A practical guide to working with angelic forces in the Hermetic tradition, with invocations, rituals and ways to fold this work into a regular spiritual practice.

books.title: Ritual: An Essential Grimoire
books.author: Damien Echols, Lorri Davis
books.description: Written with Lorri Davis, this is a beginner-friendly collection of the rituals, meditations and prayers the couple use most, for bringing magick into ordinary days.

books.title: The Alchemy of the Broken Blade: Forging Inner Transformation from the Fire of Experience
books.author: Damien Echols
books.description: His latest book brings together Hermetic alchemy and the Japanese idea of kaizen, small steady improvement, as one path of inner change. Drawing on his martial arts training, it argues for discipline, ritual and presence in everyday life. Mitch Horowitz wrote the foreword.

books.title: Life After Death
books.author: Damien Echols
books.description: His memoir of childhood in Arkansas, his wrongful conviction as a teenager and the years on death row, including the inner practices that helped him endure. It became a New York Times bestseller.

books.title: Yours for Eternity: A Love Story on Death Row
books.author: Damien Echols, Lorri Davis
books.description: Letters exchanged between Echols and Lorri Davis during his imprisonment, tracing how their relationship grew and how it sustained them both.

courses.title: Way of the Sword
courses.description: A long weekend at Omega's Rhinebeck campus that joins martial arts with spiritual discipline. Each day includes zazen, talks, and practice of a sword form from Tang Soo Do done as moving meditation, with teaching on Korean martial philosophy and inner alchemy.
courses.price: Member $445 USD, standard $495 USD (tuition; accommodation extra)

courses.title: Way of the Sword: Cutting Through Illusion (Hutton Brickyards)
courses.description: A three-day retreat on the Hudson River in Kingston, New York. Each day begins and ends with a brief talk about the Great Work, with sitting and active meditation and a wooden-sword form in between; no martial arts experience is needed.
courses.price: From $1,210 USD per person sharing or $1,384 USD single, plus tax (meals and lodging included); commuter pass $825 USD

courses.title: Damien Echols on Patreon
courses.description: A membership where he shares regular teaching on magick, meditation and practice with supporters.

Fit: ceremonial magick and Hermeticism (Qabalah, Goetia, talismans, Crowley). It is spiritual teaching in that tradition; one video title asks whether the Goetia is dangerous (it is a discussion, kept). Check you're happy with this material.
Life After Death and Yours for Eternity are memoir and letters about his wrongful conviction, not teaching; kept as his best-known books, remove if you prefer teaching books only.
The Alchemy of the Broken Blade's publisher blurb addresses readers 'shattered by trauma, by grief'; no treatment claim, and my description leaves that out. Kept.
Ritual and Yours for Eternity are co-written with his wife Lorri Davis, who has her own Patreon; not a separate listing.
The site's shop sells archangel images described as representing 'physical health' and 'healing'; not listed.
Hutton Brickyards is a hotel retreat venue; the Kingston retreat is linked on its own page.
